items.mnemonic: The SUN seen through a paper window: a square of light with one bar across the middle. Every time it climbs that window a new day starts — the sun.
ONE plank laid flat on the ground. Nothing stacked on it, nothing beside it — the first thing you can count: one.
A walled ENCLOSURE guards a single JEWEL at its center. Walls built around the treasure a people share — that is a country.
A PERSON striding away from you, two legs planted wide on the road. Just the legs are enough to know it is a person.
YEAR: a farmer bent under a heavy sheaf of rice, the harvest that comes around once in each cycle of seasons. One sheaf carried home marks one more year.
A fisherman flings both arms wide to show how BIG the one that got away was. Arms stretched as far as they will go: big.
TEN: two strokes cross at the center, one for each hand with all five fingers spread. Hands crossed, every finger counted: ten.
TWO planks laid one above the other, a short one resting on a long one. Count them: two.
A tree with a line scored across its roots — the base everything grows from. A thing with roots you can go back to and read again and again: a BOOK.
An arrow shot straight through the MIDDLE of a square target board, splitting it exactly in half. Dead center: middle.
LONG: an elder's hair flowing down past the shoulders and trailing out behind, grown over a whole lifetime. The elder leads the village, and the hair is long.
A MOUNTAIN stacked on another MOUNTAIN. The climber crests the second peak and steps out beyond the ridge into open sky — the exit.
THREE planks stacked on the ground: long, short, long. Count them: three.
The SUN hangs over the TEMPLE roof, and a monk strikes the bronze bell once for every hour. Sun over temple bell: time.
GO: a crossroads where footpaths run off to the left and the right. You stand at the center, pick one road, and go.
SEE: a huge eye walking on two legs, roaming the street to look at everything in the shop windows. An eye on legs: see.
A crescent MOON with two faint bands of cloud across its face, hanging in the night sky. Watch it wax and wane for a month — the moon.
EIGHT slices fall apart as a SWORD comes down through a round cake. Cutting the whole into pieces is to divide.
You take a STEP forward, but a tangled COCOON thread catches your WALKING LEGS and you drop back behind the group. Trailing after everyone: after.
HORNS poke up over ONE flat bar; below it a MOON and a SWORD march side by side at the head of the parade. Whatever leads the way is in front, and it got there before everyone else.
LIFE: a fresh green sprout pushing up out of the soil, one leaf already unfurled toward the light. A shoot breaking ground: life.
FIVE: an open hand held up, its fingers folded into a tidy square so it fits between two planks. One hand's worth of counting: five.
The SUN shows through the crack between the two doors of a GATE. That lit gap between the doors is the space between — an interval.
ABOVE: a baseline on the ground with a flagpole planted on it, and a flag pointing up at the sky. Everything over the line is above.
EAST: the sun rising behind a tree, caught for a moment in its branches at dawn. The side where the sun climbs the tree: east.
Inside a square ENCLOSURE a pair of LEGS kicks about. Two legs plus the two side walls they kick against: four.
NOW: a small roof with a single tag dangling under it, the present moment pinned in place before it slips away. Right here, right now.
GOLD: under a sloping roof, two bright nuggets glint in the earth beside a mine shaft. The ore everyone digs for: gold.
NINE: an elbow bent and a hand hooked at the end, holding up all its fingers but one — one short of a full pair of hands: nine.
ENTER: a tent flap pushed open, one side folded back so you can duck inside out of the rain. Step in: enter.
SMALL sparks of ideas rain down onto a COVER held over a CHILD's head, and the child under the lid soaks up every spark. That is study.
A LID caps a MOUTH on top of a FRAME that holds another MOUTH — a pagoda, story stacked on story, people calling down from each floor. Up and up: high.
YEN: a round coin stood on its edge inside a square frame — money leaning against the wall of the till. A yen coin.
CHILD: a baby wrapped tight in a blanket, both arms sticking out sideways and the legs bundled into one stroke below. A child.
In the EVENING a fortune-teller reads the DIVINATION crack in a heated shell: the answer, it says, lies outside.
EIGHT: two strokes leaning away from each other, like a fan opening or a number splitting cleanly in two. Eight.
SIX: a lid over a pair of legs — a kettle set on a hearth with its two feet planted. Lid, bar, two legs: six.
BELOW: a baseline overhead with a flagpole hanging down from it and one drop falling off the pole. Everything under the line is below.
ONE basket of RICE arrives at the door — the harvest carried in from the fields. When the rice comes, the whole family comes running: come.
STEAM rises from a rice pot, and inside the cloud a CROSS of grains swirls about. That rising vapor is the mood of the whole kitchen — spirit.
SMALL: three tiny drops, a hook in the middle and one on each side — all that is left after the big puddle dried up. Small.
SEVEN: a cross whose bottom stroke bends up into a hook, like a nail hammered in crooked. Seven.
MOUNTAIN: three peaks rising from one flat base, the middle one tallest. A mountain.
SAY the words while your TONGUE wags away — speech plus a busy tongue is talk.
WOMAN: a figure kneeling gracefully, one arm crossed in front and the skirt sweeping behind. A woman.
NORTH: two people sitting back to back, each turned away from the cold wind at their shoulders. The direction the wind comes from: north.
NOON: a sundial pole with its crossbar, casting the shortest shadow of the day straight down. Noon.
HUNDRED: one flat bar laid across a bright white sheet, a single tally stroke standing for a hundred coins. Hundred.
A BRUSH stands upright over a SUN-bright page, ink dripping down onto the paper. Brush on paper: write.
A COW on two long LEGS trots to the front of the herd and gets there first — ahead.
In the EVENING dark no one can see your face, so your MOUTH calls out who you are — your name.
RIVER: three streams of water flowing side by side down the page, the outer ones curling at the banks. A river.
THOUSAND: a tally mark slanting across the top of a ten — ten written with a flourish because it now stands for a thousand.
WATER: a central stream falling straight down with spray splashing off to both sides. Water.
HALF: a cow seen head-on, horns up, split straight down the middle by a line into two equal parts — half.
Out in the RICE FIELD, POWER drags the plow through the mud all day long. The one doing the heavy pulling: a man.
WEST: a bird settling into its nest under a horizon bar as the sun sinks. Where the sun goes down and the birds go home: west.
RAIN pours down, a SUN-bright flash splits the sky, and a FISHHOOK of lightning drops to the ground. Caught in that hook: electricity.
Under a TREE whose leaves form a LID of shade, a FATHER teaches the village children their letters — the very first school.
SAY the FIVE words every traveler's MOUTH learns first — hello, please, thank you, sorry, goodbye — and you have the start of a language.
EARTH: a mound of soil heaped on the flat ground, with a single sprout poking up out of it. Earth.
TREE: a trunk standing straight, two branches reaching out, and roots spreading wide below the ground. A tree.
An EAR pressed flat against the GATE, straining to catch the voices on the other side. Hear.
EAT: a lid resting on a heaped bowl of rice with a spoon tucked beside it. Lift the lid and eat.
CAR: a cart seen from above — an axle running through the middle, a wheel on each end, the box in between. Car.
A PERSON holds up a bent NAIL and asks with an open MOUTH: what on earth is this for? What.
SOUTH: a tent with a sheep's horns hung inside it, its door pitched to face the warm midday sun. The sunny side: south.
TEN THOUSAND: a single stroke bends and hooks like a scorpion's tail — one swarm too big for any hand to count: ten thousand.
A PERSON's hairpin sits above a MOTHER who gets up and does the same chores day after day after day — every.
WHITE: a sun with a single ray leaking off its top edge, so bright it bleaches everything around it to white.
HEAVEN: a tall figure with arms spread wide, and one flat line above its head — the sky it reaches for but cannot touch. Heaven.
MOTHER: a woman kneeling, with two dots inside the frame for the breasts that nurse the baby. Mother.
FIRE: a figure dancing around a campfire with sparks flying off on either side. Fire.
An ARM reaches down to the MOUTH with a bite of rice — the hand most people eat with: right.
SAY the words aloud: a SAMURAI stands under a COVER on his two LEGS at a market stall, reciting the scroll to the crowd — read.
An ARM reaches out and a RIGHT HAND clasps it firmly — two hands gripping across the table: friend.
An ARM holds the CRAFT tool steady while the other hand does the fine work — the steadying, helping side: left.
A PERSON leans back against a TREE in the cool shade, hat over the eyes — rest.
FATHER: two hands crossed at the wrist, gripping the stone axe of the household. Father.
RAIN: four drops falling from a cloud, caught in the panes of a window frame. Rain.
MOUTH: a square opening, wide open and waiting for the next bite. Mouth.
EYE: an eye turned on its side, the pupil a bar across the middle of the tall socket. Eye.
HAND: a palm held up with the fingers spread and the wrist trailing down below. Hand.
EAR: the outer ear with its folds drawn as bars, and a long lobe trailing down below. Ear.
FOOT: a round kneecap on top and a leg below it coming to a stop on the ground. The foot.
Under a sturdy ROOF a WOMAN rests out of the storm, safe and at peace — and the rent on this little house is cheap.
STAND a TREE upright and swing an AXE into it — fresh-cut lumber, still pale and smelling of sap: new.
A story handed down through TEN generations, each told from one MOUTH to the next — that story is old.
EVENING stacked on EVENING, the nights piling up one on another until you lose count — many.
SMALL already, and then one more STROKE is shaved off the side — even less than small: few.
SAY: a mouth at the bottom with lines of sound rising up out of it, word after word. Say.
You EAT, then tip your head back in a wide YAWN — but it is really a long, grateful gulp of cold water. Drink.
A NET full of SHELL money hauled to the market and emptied onto the counter — buy.
STAND: a figure on a baseline, arms held out and feet planted firmly apart. Stand.
A PERSON climbs up through the CLOUD to the mountaintop, where a friend is already waiting — meet.
An ALTAR built on a mound of EARTH where the whole village gathers to work and pray together — the oldest company of people.
Under a LEAN-TO roof a DIVINATION sign hangs over a MOUTH calling out today's prices — a shop.
A HORSE is measured with a RULER at the post where riders swap tired mounts for fresh ones — the station.
A ROAD winds along, and a NECK and head bob above it as a traveler walks the whole length — road.
GRASS on top; below it a PERSON stirs the soil with a SPOON until the bud changes into a flower.
